subject: zoology
question_text: Define parasitism and justify this term.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.58, VSAQ 131). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Parasitism is a close association between two
organisms of different species in which one, the
parasite, is benefited and the other, the host,
steps.why: The definition has three parts — two different species, one benefited, one harmed — and a sentence that misses any one of them is not the definition the examiner is marking.
common_mistakes: Writing only that one organism is benefited. The harm to the host is half the definition.
Calling it an association between two organisms of the SAME species.
steps.memory_tip: Two species, one gains, one is harmed. Miss the harm and it becomes commensalism.
steps.margin_note: One full sentence carrying all three parts. Do not start the example before the definition is complete.

steps.label: Justification

lines.text: Plasmodium: parasite gains, host is harmed

lines: Plasmodium vivax lives inside the liver cells
and the red blood cells of man.
It takes its food from the host and causes
The parasite is benefited and the host is
harmed, so the association is parasitism.
steps.why: A justification is not a second definition: it names one real pair and shows that in that pair one side gains and the other side is damaged.
common_mistakes: Naming the example but not saying who gains and who is harmed. The justification is the second half.
Writing 'Plasmodium' alone. Name the host as well.
steps.memory_tip: Name the pair, then say who gains and who is harmed in that same pair.
steps.margin_note: One named pair and two short lines of justification. Three lines are enough for the second mark.

insider_note: The word 'justify' is the mark: a correct definition with no worked example scores only half.
